previous_action: Gaius Maximus Valerius leads the march into the hard pass. He gives the column clear instructions to maintain formation, observe the heights, bends, side paths and concealed ground, and report any prepared killing ground before the main body commits. If an ambush is discovered, the order is not to retreat or reveal that it has been detected. Instead, the main body continues behaving as though the danger has not been noticed while Valerius sends the 300 cavalry behind the suspected ambushing force to form a closing net.

continuity.campaign_development: In October 60 BCE, Valerius personally led the expedition into the hard pass. Scouts identified a prepared ambush, and the main column continued into the pass while the 300 cavalry moved around the rear. The ambush was broken, the pass secured, and additional routes and concealed positions were documented. The expedition continues beyond the pass.
continuity.land_area_history: The personal holdings measurement remains 4.00 square miles. Round 34 involved no land acquisition, loss, transfer, or other change to the holdings.
